la:verb:malo.gloss: to prefer, want more or instead; to wish rather, choose rather
senses: to prefer, want more or instead; to wish rather, choose rather
la:verb:malo.html:
mālo, mālui, malle (old forms, mavolo for malo, ; ; ; ; ; :
mavolunt for malunt, Naev. ap. Fest. s. v. stuprum, p. 317 Müll.: mavoluit for maluit,: mavelim for malim,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; 30; 33: mavelis for malis, ; : mavelit for malit,: mavellem for mallem,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; : mavolet for malet,), v. a.
magis - volo
, to choose rather, to prefer.
In gen., constr. with acc. of the person or thing, with an object-clause, or with subj. (class.).
With acc. of the person or thing (rare): bonos et senatum malet, Cael. ap. : ambigua, ancipitia malebat,: quin omnia malit,: quod mallem,which I would prefer,; : malo, Malo Venusinam quam te,: ridenda poëmata malo, quam te,; .—In late Lat. also with acc. and dat.: ut me aliis omnibus mallet,.—
With object-clause (usu. class. constr.): seseque ii perire mavolunt ibidem, quam, etc., Naev. ap. Müll.; Enn. ap. Müll.; : Cato jam servire quam pugnare mavult,: maluit illum esse deum,; ; : judicium prius de probro quam de re maluit fieri,: praetextam sumere mavis, an esse, etc.,.—
With nom. and inf.: esse quam videri bonus malebat,: unde fit ut malim fraterculus esse gigantis,.—
With subj. (mostly poet.): mallem ... cognoscerem,: mallem divitias mihi dedisses, Quam, etc.,: fabula sit mavult, quam sine amore deus,: malo pater tibi sit Thersites,.—Sometimes with comp. abl. instead of quam (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): nullos his mallem ludos spectasse,rather than these,: ne dubitaret armis incruentas conditiones malle,to choose rather than arms, prefer to arms,.—Sometimes followed pleonastically by potius: se ab omnibus desertos potius quam abs to defensos esse malunt,: an ille Uticae potius, quam Romae, cum alienis esse quam cum suis maluisset?; id. Cat. ap. Fam. 15, 5, 2; Anton. ap. , A, 3.—Also by quam: qui magis vere vincere, quam diu imperare malit,—Strengthened by multo or haud paulo: meo judicio multo stare malo, quam aliorum,much rather,: haud paulo hunc animum malim quam, etc.,.—
In partic., to be more favorable to one: in hac re malo universae Asiae et negotiatoribus,: quamquam illi omnia malo, quam mihi,i. e. would rather he had them,.—Hence, mālens, entis, P. a., preferring (late Lat.), , ad 14, 4; Aug. c. Jul. 4, 14, 68.

senses: unpleasant to the senses, sight, smell, taste, touch
associated with bad luck, unlucky, unfavourable, unfortunate, adverse, evil
poor in condition or capacity, inept
la:adj:malus.html:
mălus, a, um, adj.
Sanscr. mala, dirt; Gr. μέλας, black; cf. macula; Germ. mal in Mutter-mal, etc.
.—
Comp.: pējor, pejus.—Sup.: pessimus, a, um, bad, in the widest sense of the word (opp. bonus), evil, wicked, injurious, destructive, mischievous, hurtful; of personal appearance, ill-looking, ugly, deformed; of weight, bad, light; of fate, evil, unlucky, etc.: malus et nequam homo,: pessima puella,; : delituit mala,: philosophi minime mali illi quidem, sed non satis acuti,: malam opinionem habere de aliquo,: consuetudo,: conscientia,: mens,: mores,: fures,: Furiae,: virus,: cicuta,: libido,: falx,: gramina,: carmen, i. e. an incantation, Leg. XII. Tab. ap. : abi in malam rem,go and be hanged!: pugna,unsuccessful, adverse,; : avis,i. e. ill-boding,; cf. : ales,: aetas, burdensome, i. e. senectus, : haud mala est mulier,not badlooking,: facies,; : crus,i. e. deformed,: pondus,i. e. light, deficient,.—Of the sick: in malis aeger est,in great danger,: tempus a quo omnis aeger pejor fiat,: eo tempore fere pessimi sunt qui aegrotant,—In neutr. sing., as adv.: ne gallina malum responset dura palato,.—Comp.: pejor, worse: via,.—Hence,
mă-lum, i, n., any thing bad, an evil, mischief, misfortune, calamity, etc.
In gen.: orarem, ut ei, quod posses mali facere, faceres,: quam sit bellum, cavere malum,: nihil enim mali accidisse Scipioni puto,: hostes inopinato malo turbati,: externum, i. e. bellum,: ne in cotidianam id malum vertat, i. e. febris,: hoc malo domitos potius cultores agrorum fore, quam, etc.,.—
In partic.
Punishment; hurt, harm, severity, injury: malo domandam tribuniciam potestatem,: malo exercitum coërcere,: sine malo,; so ; : vi, malo, plagis adductus est, ut frumenti daret,ill-usage,: amanti amoenitas malo est: nobis lucro est,is hurtful, injurious,: clementiam illi malo fuisse,was injurious, unfortunate,: malo hercle magno suo convivat sine modo, to his own

hurt, Enn. ap. (Sat. v. 1 Vahl.): olet homo quidam malo suo,: male merenti bona es: at malo cum tuo,to your own hurt,.—

Wrong-doing: causae, quae numquam malo defuturae sunt, Sen. de Ira, 1, 16, 3: sperans famam exstingui veterum sic posse malorum,; .—
As a term of abuse, plague, mischief, torment: quid tu, malum, me sequere?: qui, malum, alii?: quae, malum, est ista tanta audacia?; so ; .—
As an exclamation, alas! misery! ; Brix ad loc.—
măle, adv., badly, ill, wrongly, wickedly, unfortunately, erroneously, improperly, etc.: dubitas, quin lubenter tuo ero meus, quod possiet facere, faciat male? will do all the harm to him, etc., : si iste Italiam relinquet, faciet omnino male, et, ut ego existimo, ἀλογιστως, will act altogether unwisely, Attic. ap. : di isti Segulio male faciant,do harm to him, punish him,: o factum male de Alexione!: male velle alicui,to wish ill,: Karthagini male jamdiu cogitanti bellum multo ante denuntio, cogitare de aliquo,: male loqui,: male loqui alicui, for maledicere,: male accipere verbis aliquem,: equitatu agmen adversariorum, male habere,to harass, annoy,: hoc male habet virum,annoys, vexes him,: male se habere,to feel ill, dejected, low-spirited,: male est animo,it vexes me,: male est animo,I feel unwell,: male fit animo,I am beginning to feel bad, am getting unwell,: L. Antonio male sit, si quidem, etc., evil betide him! (a formula of imprecation), : quae res tibi vertat male,much harm may it do you!: male tibi esse malo quam molliter,I would rather you should be unfortunate than effeminate,: proelium male pugnatum,unsuccessfully,: ea quae male empta sunt,at a bad bargain,: male vendere,at a sacrifice,: male reprehendunt praemeditationem rerum futurarum,: male tegere mutationem fortunae,: male sustinere arma,unskilfully,: non dubito, quin me male oderit, i. e. very much, intensely, Caes. ap. : male metuo, ne, etc.,exceedingly, much,: rauci,miserably,.— When attached to an adjective, it freq. gives it the opposite meaning: male sanus = insanus,insane, deranged,: male sana,with mind disturbed,: gratus,i. e. ungrateful,: male fidas provincias,unfaithful,: statio male fida carinis,unsafe,.—Comp.: oderam multo pejus hunc quam illum ipsum Clodium,; cf.: pejusque leto flagitium timet,; and: cane pejus vitabit chlamydem,.

la:noun:malum.gloss: evil, adversity, hardship, misfortune, calamity, disaster, mischief
senses: evil, adversity, hardship, misfortune, calamity, disaster, mischief
la:noun:malum.html:
mālum, i, n., = μῆλον (Doric μᾶ λον),
an apple, i. e. any tree-fruit fleshy on the outside, and having a kernel within (opp. nux); hence, applied also to quinces, pomegranates, peaches, oranges, lemons, etc.
In gen., ; ; : malis orbiculatis pasci, Cael. ad .—In a pun with mălum, a calamity, ; —Prov.: ab ovo usque ad mala, i. e. from beginning to end (from the Roman custom to begin meals with eggs and end with fruit), .—Trop.: malum discordiae,an apple of discord,.—
Malum terrae, a plant (the Aristolochia), having four varieties, ; ; also called malum terrenum,.

senses: a standard or pole to which the awnings spread over the theater were attached
the beam in the middle of a winepress
the corner beams of a tower
la:noun:malus.html:
mālus, i, f., Gr. μηλέα,
an appletree: malus bifera,: et steriles platani malos gessere valentes,: malus granata,the pomegranate,: felices arbores putantur esse quercus...malus, etc.,.

senses: any tree fruit with a fleshy exterior, e.g. quinces, pears, peaches, etc.

la:noun:mala.html:
māla, ae, f.
mando, like scala, from scando
,
the cheek-bone, jaw; in the stricter anatomical sense, the upper bones of the face, between the eyes, nose, and mouth, in which the teeth are fixed (usually in plur.): maxilla est mobile os. Malae cum toto osse, quod superiores dentes excipit, immobiles sunt,: dentium pars maxillae, pars superiori ossi malarum haeret,: ut meos malis miser manderem natos, Poët. ap. ; : ambesas subigat malis absumere mensas,.—Of the dog, ; of the horse,; of the wolf,; of the lion: horribilique malā,.—
Transf., the corresponding external part of the face, a cheek (mostly in plur.): infra oculos malae homini tantum, quas prisci genas vocabant Pudoris haec sedes: ibi maxime ostenditur rubor,: pugno malam si tibi percussero mox,; : feri malam illi rursum,slap his cheek again,: (juventas) molli vestit lanugine malas,; ; : impubes,: tenerae,: Quod Aulo Agerio a Numerio Negidio pugno mala percussa est, Vet. Form. in Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 2, 7, 4: paucae sine vulnere malae,.

la:adj:malitiosus.html:
mălĭtĭōsus, a, um, adj.
malitia
,
full of wickedness, wicked, knavish, crafty, malicious.
In gen. (class.): homo,: malitiosissimus,.—Of things: juris interpretatio,.—
As nom. prop.: Silva Malitiosa,a forest in the Sabine territory,; = ὕλη κακοῦργος, Dion. 3, 33. —Hence, adv.: mălĭtĭōsē, wickedly, knavishly, perfidiously: quicquam agi dolose, aut malitiose,: facere aliquid,.—Comp.: rem mandatam malitiosius gerere,.

senses: spite, malice, ill will; an act of malice
la:noun:malitia.html:
mălĭtĭa, ae, f.
malus
,
bad quality, badness.
Lit. (post-class.): terrae malitia,: arboris,unfruitfulness,.—
Trop., ill-will, spite, malice (class.): virtutis contraria est vitiositas: sic enim malo, quam malitiam, appellare eam, quam Graeci κακίαν appellant: nam malitia certi cujusdam vitii nomen est: vitiositas omnium,: est enim malitia versuta et fallax nocendi ratio,; : per summam fraudem et malitiam,; ; opp. to virtus: virtute, non malitia, P. Scipioni placuisse,.—With malus: sine mala omni malitia,.—In plur.: collatio nostrarum malitiarum,: everriculum malitiarum omnium,.—
Cunning, artfulness: muliebris malitia adhibenda est mihi,.—
Sometimes in a good sense, like our roguery, : tamen a malitia non discedis,you do not desist from your roguery,.

la:noun:malevolentia.html:
mălĕvŏlentīa (mălĭv-), ae, f.
malevolens
,
ill-will, evil disposition towards any one, dislike, hatred, envy, malevolence (class.): malevolentia est voluptas ex malo alterius sine emolumento suo,: malevolentia in ceteros,: obtrectatio et malevolentia,: malevolentia et invidia,: vicinitas non infuscata malevolentia,.

la:adj:malevolens.html:
mălĕvŏlens (mălĭvŏl-), entis, adj.
male-volens
,
ill-disposed, disaffected, envious, spiteful, malevolent (very rare, and in posit. ante-class.): est miserorum ut malevolentes sint,: ingenium,.—Sup.: malevolentissimae obtrectationes,; . 17.—As subst.: mălĕvŏlens, entis, m., a spiteful person, an enemy: jam meo malost quod malevolentes gaudeant,: (manu) malam rem mittunt malevolentibus,.

la:adj:malignus.html:
mălignus, a, um, adj.
for maligenus, malus, and gen-, root of gigno; cf. the opp. benignus
,
of an evil nature or disposition, ill-disposed, wicked, mischievous, malicious, spiteful, envious, malignant, malign (poet. and post-Aug.; syn.: invidus, malevolus, parcus).
In gen.: maligni caupones,: magnaque numinibus vota exaudita malignis,unkind,.— Of inanim. and abstr. things: malignissima capita,: litus,: portus,: leges,: votum,: verba,: mente malignā,: studia,: vulgus,: oculi,.—
In partic.
Stingy, niggardly: malignus, largus,.—Of favors, : vagae ne parce malignus arenae ossibus particulam dare, .—Trop.: fama,: in laudandis dictionibus,.—
Transf.
Barren, unfruitful: terra malignior ceteris,: colles,.—
Scanty, insufficient, dim, petty, small, narrow: ostium,too narrow,: aditus,: ignis,: lux,: conspecta est parva maligna Unda procul venā,: munus,.—Hence, adv.: mălignē.
In gen., ill-naturedly, spitefully, enviously, malignantly (not in Cic. or Cæs.): maledice ac maligne loqui,.—Comp.: malignius habitum esse sermonem,.—
In partic.
Stingily, grudgingly: ager maligne plebi divisus,: famem exstinguere,sparingly,: non mihi fuit tam maligne, ut, etc., it has not gone so poorly with me that, etc., : dispensare,: laudare,.—Comp.: dicis, malignius tecum egisse naturam,.—
Little, scantily: terra eorum, quae seruntur, maligne admodum patiens,a very little,: apertus,: virens,.

la:verb:maligno.html:
măligno, 1, v. a., and mălignor, ātus, 1, v. dep.
id.
,
to do or contrive maliciously, to malign (post-class.).
Form maligno: consilium super populum tuum,: venena malignantes,i. e. maliciously ejecting,.—
Form malignor: quanta malignatus est inimicus in sancto,: in prophetis meis nolite malignari,; 37, 8 sq.—P. a. as subst.: mălignan-tes, ium, m., the wicked,

la:adj:malesuadus.html:
mălĕsuādus, a, um, adj.
male-suadeo
,
ill-advising, seductive (poet.): Illa hanc corrumpit mulierem viti malesuada plena, Lorenz ad loc. (al. vitilena): interpres,.— Transf., of inanim. and abstr. things; of wine: malesuadi pocula succi,: Fames,.

la:adj:malifer.html:
mālĭfer, fĕra, fĕrum, adj.
malumfero
,
apple-bearing (poet.): Et quos maliferae despectant moenia Abellae,.

la:verb:maledico.html:
mălĕdīco (or separately, mălĕ dīco;
rarely in reverse order: qui bonis dicunt male,; cf. ), xi. ctum, 3, v. n. and a. [male-dico], to speak ill of, to abuse, revile, slander, asperse; constr. absol., or with a dat. (so class.) or acc. (post-Aug.).
Absol.: aliud est maledicere, aliud accusare,.—
With dat.: optimo viro maledicere,: turpissime alicui,: petulanter alicui,: utrique,: Christo,; .—Impers. pass.: indignis si maledicitur, maledictum id esse dico,; . —
With acc.: si me amas, maledic illam,; v. .—
Esp., to curse, utter a curse upon (eccl. Lat.): populo huic,—Hence,
mălĕdī-cens, entis, P. a., evil - speaking, foulmouthed, abusive, scurrilous (syn. maledi cus): maledicentes homines,.—Comp.: maledicentior,.—Sup.: in maledicentissimā civitate,: carmina,; .—
mălĕdictus, a, um, P. a., accursed (post-class. for exsecrabilis): maledicte parricida,: maledictus es inter omnia animantia,: omnes incesti, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 6, 7 praef.—Hence, as subst.: mălĕ-dictum, i, n., a foul or abusive word.
In gen. (class.): maledicta in aliquem dicere,: in vitam alicujus conicere,: maledictis figere aliquem,: maledicta in aliquem conferre,: quod crimen (i. e. majestatis) non solum facto, sed et verbis impiis ac maledictis maxime exacerbatur,.—
In partic., a curse, imprecation: esse in maledictis jam antiquis strigem, convenit,: scribere maledicta,.—
Transf., a cursed thing: Christus factus pro nobis maledictum,: maledictum non erit amplius,.

la:adj:malacus.html:
mălăcus, a, um, adj., = μαλακός,
soft, supple, pliant (Plautin.): pallium malacum et calidum,: pallium,.—
Transf., soft, delicate, luxurious: ad saltandum malacus,: unctiones,: in malacum modum,.

la:verb:malefacio.html:
mălĕfăcĭo (or separately, mălĕ fă-cio), fēci, factum, 3, v. n.
male-facio
,
to do evil, harm, mischief to any one, to injure: alicui,: neque tu verbis solves umquam, quod mi re male feceris,: tibi,.—With contra: malefacere omnia contra aliquem,.—Hence, mălĕfactum (or separately, mălĕ factum; sync., malfactum, ; v. Ritschl, Opusc. 2, p. 720 sq.), i, n., an evil deed, injury: benefacta male locata malefacta arbitror, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 429 Vahl.): augere,.

la:adj:maledicus.html:
mălĕdĭcus, a, um, adj.
maledico
,
foul-mouthed, abusive, scurrilous, slanderous (class.): conviciator maledicus,: homines,: maledicum esse in aliquem,. —Transf., of inanim. and abstr. things: civitas,: lingua,: sermo,.—Hence, adv.: mă-lĕdĭcē, in a slanderous manner, abusively, scurrilously: maledice contumelioseque dicere,; so, maledice ac maligne loqui,.

la:noun:maleficium.gloss: crime, misdeed, offence, evil deed, wrong, mischief
senses: crime, misdeed, offence, evil deed, wrong, mischief
la:noun:maleficium.html:
mălĕfĭcĭum, ĭi, n.
maleficus
,
an evil deed, misdeed, wickedness, offence, crime.
Lit.
In gen. (class.): ne conscii sint ipsi malefici suis,: conscientia maleficiorum,: committere, admittere,to commit,: exsilio multare,: supplicia pro maleficiis metuere,.—
In partic. (mostly post-Aug.).
Fraud, deception, adulteration: me maleficio vinceres? Speng.; ; .—
Enchantment, sorcery, Orell. N. cr.; ; ; cf. magica,; Schol. .—
Transf., mischief, hurt, harm, injury, wrong inflicted (acc. to maleficus, II.): pro maleficio beneficium reddere,: ab injuria et maleficio se prohibere,: sine ullo maleficio,; : novis corrumperent maleficiis,: maleficii occasione omissa, —Hence, transf. (abstr. pro concr.), a noxious insect, vermin: ita non nasci maleficia,; ; .

la:noun:malignitas.html:
mălignĭtas, ātis, f.
malignus
.
ill-will, spite, malice, envy, malignity (not in Cic. or Cæs.).—Lit.: malignitati falsa species libertatis inest,: malignitas multo veneno tincta,: interpretantium,: humana,: malignitas et livor,.—In plur.: malignitatum vulnera, Prud. στεφ. 2, 259.—
Stinginess, niggardliness, meanness [v. malignus, II.]: ita malignitate oneravit omnes mortales mihi,; ; ; .—Hence,
Transf., stingy or niggardly act: malignitatis auctores quaerendo,: accensaque ea cupiditas est malignitate patrum,.—
Barrenness, unfruitfulness; of the vine, .

la:adj:maleficus.html:
mălĕfĭcus (in MSS. also mălĭfĭ-cus), a, um, adj.
malefacio
,
evil-doing, nefarious, vicious, wicked, criminal.
Lit.
In gen. (class.): homo natura maleficus, et injustus,: malefici sceleratique homines,: maleficentissimus,: mores malefici,: malefica vita,.—As subst.: mălĕ-fĭous, i, m., an evil-doer, criminal: contra istoc detrudi maleficos Aequom videlur,.—
In partic., magical: artes,.—As substt.
mălĕfĭcus, i, m., a magician, enchanter: de maleficis et mathematicis,: magi qui malefici vulgi consuetudine nuncupantur,; Schol. .—
mălĕfĭcum, i, n., a charm, means of enchantment: semusti cineres aliaque malefica, quis creditur anima numinibus inferis sacrari,—
Transf., hurtful, injurious, noxious, mischievous (only post-Aug.): Christiani, genus hominum superstitionis novae atque maleficae,: sidera,: vis,: bestia piscibus malefica,: caprae, maleficum frondibus animal,: natura,inimical, unpropitious,: bestia,.— Hence, adv.: mălĕfĭcē, mischievously: aliquid agere,.

la:adj:malevolus.html:
mălĕvŏlus (mălĭv-), a, um, adj.

Lit.: (navis) excussa malleo,: malleorum rostra,: stuparius,a swingle-staff,.—Of the maul or axe for felling animals to be sacrificed: tempora discussit claro cava malleus ictu,: elato alte malleo, cultrarium mactavit,.—Prov.: malleum sapientiorem vidi excusso manubrio,the hammer wiser than the handle,.—
Transf., a disease among animals: sunt species mallei septem,; .

senses: A mallet-shoot or hammer-shaped slip or cutting; literally, a “little hammer.” A propagation method where a young, green shoot is harvested with a small, horizontal section of the older, woody branch still attached at the base. This “T” junction resembles a mallet — the older wood forms the “head” and the new shoot forms the “handle” — providing a sturdy, nutrient-rich base for new roots to develop.
The tongue of a shoe buckle.
